findings.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId reads substring(3, 5) instead of the grant field at substring(4, 6) and rejects equality, allowing tokens with the wrong grant shortcut when the suffix is a UUID
OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut permits three-character shortcuts, but decoding requires exactly two grant characters, allowing extensions to mint token IDs the framework cannot decode

The late-deployment refresh path inserts grant mappings without checking shortcut uniqueness, allowing a new grant to overwrite an existing shortcut and previously issued tokens to decode as the wrong grant
AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null raw IDs to encode as token IDs ending in :null

DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType encounters an NPE from an uninitialized sessionFactory before the intended IllegalArgumentException, while its broad RuntimeException catch incorrectly treats the fixture failure as success

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut permits three-character shortcuts, but decoding requires exactly two grant characters, allowing extensions to mint token IDs the framework cannot decode

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is documented as returning 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoding logic in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() expects exactly 6 characters total for the encoded context (2 for sessionType, 2 for tokenType, 2 for grantType). The code at line 79-84 explicitly checks 'if (encodedContext.length() != 6)' and extracts grant type shortcut as 'encodedContext.substring(4, 6)' - exactly 2 characters. All factory implementations in the diff use 2-character shortcuts ('ac', 'cc', 'pg', 'pc', 'rt', 'ro', 'te', 'ci', 'dg'). If an extension provides a 3-character shortcut as the Javadoc suggests is acceptable, encoding would produce a 7-character prefix, and decoding would fail with 'Incorrect token id' or extract wrong characters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The late-deployment refresh path inserts grant mappings without checking shortcut uniqueness, allowing a new grant to overwrite an existing shortcut and previously issued tokens to decode as the wrong grant

adjudication.rationale: Looking at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java, the getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut methods add new mappings to grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts when a new grant type is discovered at runtime. These methods use ConcurrentHashMap.put() which will overwrite existing entries if a new grant has the same shortcut as an existing one. While postInit() validates uniqueness at startup, the late-deployment refresh paths (lines 107-111 and 125-131) do not check for shortcut collisions before inserting. If a dynamically deployed grant has a duplicate shortcut, it would overwrite the existing mapping, causing previously issued tokens to decode with the wrong grant type.
